subject: Qualify: availability expectations + failover tests for NextGen Retail POC
messages:
From: Erica Morales <emorales@nextgenretail.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@nextgenretail.com>, procurement@nextgenretail.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Qualify: availability expectations + failover tests for NextGen Retail POC

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for the call earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a few follow-ups so my CTO (Tom) and procurement can align: 

- We're trying to validate both latency and availability under promotional load spikes (Black Friday-style bursts). Our internal SLO target is 99.95% per-month for tail latency < 200ms for inferencing the recommendation model.
- Key question: how does Redwood handle instantaneous region failover and what are expected RTO/RPO? We heard about routing policies and automatic fallbacks on the call but want concrete behavior vs AWS/GCP endpoints.
- We're also tracking rate limiting: if we burst to 5x baseline QPS for 3–5 minutes, will requests be dropped, throttled, or queued? What sort of token/account-level limits apply?

Can you send a short doc that maps behavior to: AWS SageMaker endpoints, Google Vertex, and Azure OpenAI (managed endpoints) — especially on multi-region failover and error budgets? Also please include any test plan we can run during the POC so our infra team can simulate failover.

I've attached our SLA_requirements.pdf for reference.

Thanks,
Erica
VP Product
NextGen Retail

[Attachment: SLA_requirements.pdf (pdf)]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Erica Morales <emorales@nextgenretail.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@nextgenretail.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 18:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Qualify: availability expectations + failover tests for NextGen Retail POC

Erica — really helpful — thanks for the clear goals and the SLA doc. Attaching a concise POC test plan and a one-page matrix that compares expected behaviors across Redwood vs the major hyperscalers. Highlights:

- Multi-region failover: Redwood supports active-active routing with health-based routing and automated model-variant fallback. Typical RTO observed in our POCs: 20–45s for cross-region failover when KV-cache warm start is required; if using our prefix-caching mode and warm standby, failover can be under 10s. Hyperscaler managed endpoints often rely on DNS TTL and load balancer reconfiguration — in practice that introduces 30–120s depending on cache TTLs and their chosen front-door.
- Error budgets & SLOs: we can commit to operational SLOs for Dedicated customers. For hosted POC we provide a reliability profile and recommend embedding graceful degradation: token-level retries + lower-cost fallback model variants.
- Rate limiting: Redwood offers per-account and per-route burst policies. On a 5x burst for <5 minutes we typically queue up to configured max queue depth (configurable) rather than dropping, with circuit-breaker thresholds to fail fast after sustained overload. Hyperscalers typically return 429s when throttled.

Next actions I propose:
1) Monica to share the POC Test Plan (attached) with exact commands and curl examples for load gen.
2) Redwood runs a short failover demo (we can simulate an AZ+region ejection) w/ your infra — propose Thu 4/15 10:00 PT.
3) Provide a short XLS mapping with measured averages across our internal benchmarks vs public hyperscaler docs.

Attachments: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-quick-metrics.xlsx, POC-test-plan.md

— Karthik
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-quick-metrics.xlsx (xls)]

From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Erica Morales <emorales@nextgenretail.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@nextgenretail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: POC test plan + concrete commands (next steps)

Hi Erica / Tom —

Attaching the POC test plan with exact steps. High-level notes:

- Step 1 (baseline): 10 minutes of steady load at expected production QPS (curl examples in section 2). Measure 95/99/99.9 tail latencies and error rate.
- Step 2 (burst): ramp to 5x for 5 minutes, then return to baseline. Repeat 3x. We will observe queueing behavior and whether responses are delayed vs 429s.
- Step 3 (region ejection): our ops team will simulate regional ejection by blocking region endpoint for 60s; your infra will continue to send traffic to the same DNS target to observe client-side behavior; we will record RTO and cold-cache penalty.
- Step 4 (failback & warm standby): enable prefix caching / warm standby for an additional run to show improved RTO.

Expected deliverables from Redwood POC run:
- Timeline of observed failover (RTO) and tail latencies for each step
- Error budget consumption during the test window
- Packet with configuration recommendations (queue depth, retry backoff, model-variant mapping)

Proposed demo: Thu 2026-04-15 10:00 PT. Please confirm who from your infra will be on the call and whether we should include a vendor contact (hyperscaler) for side-by-side checks.

Thanks,
Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: POC-test-plan.md (text)]

From: Erica Morales <emorales@nextgenretail.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@nextgenretail.com>, procurement@nextgenretail.com, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC test plan + concrete commands (next steps)

Thanks Karthik/Monica — this looks good. Confirming Thu 4/15 10:00 PT. Tom (cc) will lead infra; procurement copied for timing on the trial agreement. A couple quick clarifications before the demo: 

- For the comparison matrix, can you add a row that explicitly calls out "DNS TTL dependence" vs "active route health checks"? That was a key distinction for our network team.
- We want to see what happens to in-flight requests during failover (drop vs retry vs requeue). Please instrument traces so we can see per-request path.

Procurement: we'll need a short statement of Redwood's reliability profile for POC (can be non-binding) and an estimate of expected monthly error-budget impact if we run production-like traffic for the month.

Looking forward — see you Thursday.

Erica
VP Product
NextGen Retail
